topic.readerProblem: A founder or marketer wants to know which factors make ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude and Google AI cite a page or name a brand, and which of the many published ranking-factor lists can be trusted.
topic.connection: AEOeye audits whether AI engines name a brand for buyer questions. This page sorts every commonly cited factor into documented, measured and inferred, ties the documented access gate to AEOeye's crawler access study, and uses the recommendation benchmark (with its caveats) to explain why being named at all is the hard part.

assessment: The page replaces an opinion-ranked list with an evidence-graded one: ten factors in a ranked table with a grade column, then separate sections for what OpenAI, Perplexity, Anthropic and Google document, what three studies measured (GEO, University of Toronto, GEO-16) with their design limits, and what remains inference (entity clarity, backlinks, structured data, llms.txt). It deliberately drops the earlier Semrush Reddit/Wikipedia/YouTube citation shares and the claim that ChatGPT leans on Bing, which it could not verify from primary pages, and it states no ranking weights because no engine publishes any.

sources.supports: Google's AI features use retrieval from the Search index and query fan-out; unique, non-commodity content will likely matter most; llms.txt, chunking, inauthentic mentions and special markup are not needed; structured data is not required; no third-party tool has access to Google's internal ranking or AI systems.
To be a supporting link in AI Overviews or AI Mode a page must be indexed and eligible to be shown in Google Search with a snippet.
Google-Extended controls use of crawled content for Gemini training and grounding and does not affect inclusion in Google Search.
Organization structured data on the home page can help Google better understand and disambiguate an organization in search results.
OAI-SearchBot surfaces sites in ChatGPT search; opted-out sites are not shown in ChatGPT search answers but can appear as navigational links; GPTBot (training) is a separate setting.
PerplexityBot surfaces and links sites in Perplexity search results and is not used to crawl content for AI foundation models.
Disabling Claude-SearchBot prevents indexing for search and may reduce visibility and accuracy in Claude search results.

Microsoft (October 2025): crawlability, metadata, internal linking and backlinks remain essential for discoverability; Copilot-style assistants break content into smaller pieces; schema markup is recommended.

GEO (KDD 2024): GEO-bench of 10K queries (1K test split); statistics, quotations and cited sources gave 30-40% (position-adjusted word count) and 15-30% (subjective impression) relative gains; keyword stuffing little to none; Perplexity.ai table: quotation addition 29.1 vs 24.1 baseline, keyword stuffing 21.9.

University of Toronto: data collected August 2025; US software-product queries 72.7% earned / 26.7% brand for a search-enabled GPT vs Google 45.4% earned / 43.7% brand; engines differ in domain diversity and freshness; AI search deprioritized community platforms such as Reddit in consumer electronics.

GEO-16: 1,100 URLs, 1,702 citations from Brave Summary, Google AI Overviews and Perplexity for 70 product-intent prompts on B2B SaaS pages; metadata and freshness (r=0.68), semantic HTML (0.65), structured data (0.63) most associated with citation; observational design with possible confounding.
AI search answers vary across runs, prompts and time, so one-off observations are unreliable and visibility should be measured as a distribution.
